cards.back: An animal with a backbone.
cards.say: vertebrate. An animal with a backbone.

cards.back: An animal with no backbone.
cards.say: invertebrate. An animal with no backbone.

cards.back: A line of small bones called vertebrae down the middle of the back. It is also called the spine.
cards.say: backbone. A line of small bones called vertebrae down the middle of the back. It is also called the spine.

cards.front: Name the five groups of vertebrates.
cards.back: Mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish.
cards.say: Name the five groups of vertebrates. Mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and fish.

cards.back: A vertebrate with hair or fur. Babies drink milk from their mother, and most mammals give birth to live young.
cards.say: mammal. A vertebrate with hair or fur. Babies drink milk from their mother, and most mammals give birth to live young.

cards.back: A vertebrate with feathers, wings and a beak. Birds lay eggs with hard shells.
cards.say: bird. A vertebrate with feathers, wings and a beak. Birds lay eggs with hard shells.

cards.back: A vertebrate with dry, scaly skin. Most reptiles lay eggs with leathery shells. Snakes and lizards are reptiles.
cards.say: reptile. A vertebrate with dry, scaly skin. Most reptiles lay eggs with leathery shells. Snakes and lizards are reptiles.

cards.back: A vertebrate with moist, smooth skin. Young ones live in water and adults often live on land. Frogs are amphibians.
cards.say: amphibian. A vertebrate with moist, smooth skin. Young ones live in water and adults often live on land. Frogs are amphibians.

cards.back: A vertebrate with scales and fins that lives in water and breathes using gills.
cards.say: fish. A vertebrate with scales and fins that lives in water and breathes using gills.

cards.back: An animal whose body stays at about the same temperature, however warm or cold it is outside. Mammals and birds are warm-blooded.
cards.say: warm-blooded. An animal whose body stays at about the same temperature, however warm or cold it is outside. Mammals and birds are warm-blooded.

cards.back: An animal whose body temperature changes with its surroundings. Fish, amphibians and reptiles are cold-blooded.
cards.say: cold-blooded. An animal whose body temperature changes with its surroundings. Fish, amphibians and reptiles are cold-blooded.

cards.back: Organs that fish use to take oxygen from the water.
cards.say: gills. Organs that fish use to take oxygen from the water.

cards.back: No. A bat is a mammal. It has fur and feeds its babies milk.
cards.say: Is a bat a bird? No. A bat is a mammal. It has fur and feeds its babies milk.

cards.back: No. A whale is a mammal. It breathes air with lungs and feeds its calf milk.
cards.say: Is a whale a fish? No. A whale is a mammal. It breathes air with lungs and feeds its calf milk.

cards.front: Which vertebrate group does a frog belong to?
cards.back: Amphibians.
cards.say: Which vertebrate group does a frog belong to? Amphibians.

cards.front: Which vertebrate group does a crocodile belong to?
cards.back: Reptiles.
cards.say: Which vertebrate group does a crocodile belong to? Reptiles.

cards.front: What are some groups of invertebrates?
cards.back: Insects, spiders, worms, snails and slugs, and crabs and prawns.
cards.say: What are some groups of invertebrates? Insects, spiders, worms, snails and slugs, and crabs and prawns.

cards.back: An invertebrate with six legs and three body parts: head, thorax and abdomen. Most have wings.
cards.say: insect. An invertebrate with six legs and three body parts: head, thorax and abdomen. Most have wings.

cards.front: How many legs does a spider have?
cards.back: Eight. A spider has two body parts, not three.
cards.say: How many legs does a spider have? Eight. A spider has two body parts, not three.

cards.back: An invertebrate with a soft body, often with a shell. Snails and squid are molluscs.
cards.say: mollusc. An invertebrate with a soft body, often with a shell. Snails and squid are molluscs.

cards.back: An invertebrate with a hard outer shell and many jointed legs. Crabs and prawns are crustaceans.
cards.say: crustacean. An invertebrate with a hard outer shell and many jointed legs. Crabs and prawns are crustaceans.

cards.back: A hard covering on the outside of the body. Insects and crabs have one.
cards.say: exoskeleton. A hard covering on the outside of the body. Insects and crabs have one.

cards.front: Which is an invertebrate: a snail or a lizard?
cards.back: A snail. A lizard has a backbone.
cards.say: Which is an invertebrate: a snail or a lizard? A snail. A lizard has a backbone.

cards.back: To sort living things into groups using their features.
cards.say: classify. To sort living things into groups using their features.
